why: The authors' complete C implementation, Makefile, benchmark drivers, and the required words_alpha.txt are present in the cloned repository. The match target C1 is produced by the included chaining_benchmark binary; only environment setup (a C toolchain/make on Windows) is needed.
blockers_seen: Windows 11 does not ship POSIX make/cc by default; MinGW-w64/MSYS2 or WSL is needed to run the Makefile
The benchmark is single-threaded and CPU-bound, so extra CPU cores do not reduce C1 runtime

feasibility.est_runtime_on_this_machine: about 10-18 min for a full C1 run; about 20-35 min if the clean re-run is also full
feasibility.scale_down_plan: Keep the 500k-key insert because it determines the exact 31,250.5 chain length, but sample e.g. 100k random successful lookups for the verification run; the expected average remains ~31,250 with roughly ±60 sampling noise. A 250k-key run would be ~4x cheaper but yields ~15,625, so it cannot reproduce C1.

compute.basis: C1 is one single-threaded C benchmark; the paper reports 271.5 s insert + 338.3 s lookup on an M4 Pro, so ~10 min per full run and roughly 20-30 min including a clean second run on a reference laptop.
